Definition: from the same as G2226 and a derivative of G1096; to engender alive, i.e. (by analogy) to rescue (passively, be saved) from death:--live, preserve.
BiblicalUsage: Zoogoneo means to preserve alive, to rescue from death — whoever seeks to save his life shall lose it, Jesus says, and whoever loses it shall preserve it alive. Pharaoh's Egypt tried the opposite, forcing the Hebrew babies to be cast out so they would not be preserved alive, while God kept His people through it. Paul charges Timothy before God, 'who quickeneth all things,' to keep the commandment without spot.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God alone is the one who gives life and keeps it — Pharaoh could order death, but he could not stop God from preserving a people, and he cannot stop God from preserving me. Losing my life for Christ's sake is the only way to keep it.
